title: Mom knows this tune
setting: A rainy Saturday at home. Kenji's soccer with his friends is rained off, so he has been on his video game all morning when his mother comes into the living room, where the old family piano stands.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.ja: ケンジ、まだゲームしてるの？
lines.kana: けんじ、まだげーむしてるの？
lines.english: Kenji, are you still on that game?

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: うん。だって、雨降ってるし。
lines.kana: うん。だって、あめふってるし。

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.ja: 今日はサッカーしないの？
lines.kana: きょうはさっかーしないの？

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: shinai yo. minna mo uchi de geemu shiteru.
lines.ja: しないよ。みんなも家でゲームしてる。
lines.kana: しないよ。みんなもうちでげーむしてる。
lines.english: Nope. Everyone else is at home gaming too.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: jaa, piano hiite miru? mukashi naratteta n da kara.
lines.ja: じゃあ、ピアノ弾いてみる？昔習ってたんだから。
lines.kana: じゃあ、ぴあのひいてみる？むかしならってたんだから。
lines.english: Then why not have a go on the piano? You took lessons, after all.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: naratteta kedo, mou hikenai yo. zutto hiitenai shi.
lines.ja: 習ってたけど、もう弾けないよ。ずっと弾いてないし。
lines.kana: ならってたけど、もうひけないよ。ずっとひいてないし。
lines.english: I did, but I can't play anymore. I haven't touched it in ages.

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: okaasan mo mukashi, piano naratteta n da yo.
lines.ja: お母さんも昔、ピアノ習ってたんだよ。
lines.kana: おかあさんもむかし、ぴあのならってたんだよ。
lines.english: I took piano lessons too, you know, back in the day.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e, honto ni? okaasan, piano hikeru no?
lines.ja: え、ほんとに？お母さん、ピアノ弾けるの？
lines.kana: え、ほんとに？おかあさん、ぴあのひけるの？
lines.english: Wait, really? Mom, you can play the piano?

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: hikeru yo. jaa, chotto hiku ne.
lines.ja: 弾けるよ。じゃあ、ちょっと弾くね。
lines.kana: ひけるよ。じゃあ、ちょっとひくね。
lines.english: Of course I can. Here, I'll play you a bit.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: e! sore, kono geemu no kyoku da!
lines.ja: え！それ、このゲームの曲だ！
lines.kana: え！それ、このげーむのきょくだ！
lines.english: Whoa! That's the music from this game!

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: un. kenji ga zutto geemu shiteru kara, oboechatta.
lines.ja: うん。ケンジがずっとゲームしてるから、覚えちゃった。
lines.kana: うん。けんじがずっとげーむしてるから、おぼえちゃった。
lines.english: Yep. You're on that game all the time, so I picked it up.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: お母さん、めっちゃ上手だね。
lines.kana: おかあさん、めっちゃじょうずだね。

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: kenji mo hiite miru? oshieru yo.
lines.ja: ケンジも弾いてみる？教えるよ。
lines.kana: けんじもひいてみる？おしえるよ。
lines.english: Want to try playing it? I'll teach you.

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.romaji: un! a, ame yanda. jaa, sakkaa suru!
lines.ja: うん！あ、雨やんだ。じゃあ、サッカーする！
lines.kana: うん！あ、あめやんだ。じゃあ、さっかーする！
lines.english: Yeah! Oh, the rain's stopped. Right, I'm off to play soccer!

lines.speaker: kenji
lines.ja: 明日弾く！行ってきます！
lines.kana: あしたひく！いってきます！

lines.speaker: okaasan
lines.romaji: hai hai. ki o tsukete ne.
lines.ja: はいはい。気をつけてね。
lines.kana: はいはい。きをつけてね。

choices.english: Kenji's mom finds out he can still play the piano, and he plays her the music from his game before going out to play soccer.
Kenji's mom tells him to stop gaming and go to his piano lesson, but he goes to play soccer with his friends instead.
Kenji is gaming because of the rain. His mom plays his game's music on the piano and offers to teach him, but when the rain stops he runs off to play soccer.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-4: soccer is off because it's raining (ame futteru shi, sakkaa shinai no? / shinai yo), so Kenji is gaming. Lines 7-9: his mom took piano lessons too (piano naratteta) and can still play (hikeru yo). Lines 10-11: what she plays is the music from his game, which she picked up from hearing it all the time. Line 13: she offers to teach him (oshieru yo). Lines 14-16: the rain stops (ame yanda), he goes to play soccer (sakkaa suru!) and puts the piano off till tomorrow (ashita hiku!). A is wrong: Kenji says he can't play anymore (line 6: mou hikenai yo), and it's his mom who plays. B is wrong: there's no lesson today. The lessons were long ago (mukashi naratteta), and his mom only suggests he try the piano at home.

questions.english: Kenji is amazed that his mom can play the music from his game. She says "kenji ga zutto geemu shiteru kara, oboechatta." How does she know the tune?
questions.ja: なんでお母さんはこの曲が弾けるんですか？
questions.kana: なんでおかあさんはこのきょくがひけるんですか？
questions.romaji: nande okaasan wa kono kyoku ga hikeru n desu ka?

choices.english: Kenji is on that game all the time, and she picked the tune up from hearing it.
She plays the game herself when Kenji isn't around.
She learned it in her piano lessons years ago.

questions.explanation: Line 11: kenji ga zutto geemu shiteru is 'Kenji is gaming all the time': geemu (o) suru in its -teru form, with zutto for 'constantly'. Because the game music is always on, it stuck (oboechatta). B is wrong: kenji ga makes Kenji the one gaming, not her. C mixes up the two kinds of learning: she did take piano lessons as a girl (line 7: piano naratteta), but she picked this tune up by ear, which is oboeru, not narau.

questions.english: Kenta asks, "kinou, nani shiteta?" (What were you up to yesterday?) You spent the day playing soccer with friends. Tell him.
questions.answer: Say you were playing soccer, using sakkaa with suru in its -teta form: tomodachi to sakkaa shiteta yo.

modelAnswers.ja: 友達とサッカーしてたよ。
modelAnswers.english: I was playing soccer with friends.

modelAnswers.romaji: kinou wa tomodachi to sakkaa o shitemashita.
modelAnswers.ja: 昨日は友達とサッカーをしてました。
modelAnswers.english: Yesterday I was playing soccer with friends.

questions.explanation: A sport takes suru: sakkaa (o) suru, with o usually dropped in casual talk, as in line 3 (kyou wa sakkaa shinai no?) and line 14 (jaa, sakkaa suru!). Shiteta is 'was doing'. Don't let English 'play' pull you to asobu: sakkaa o asobu isn't Japanese, and tomodachi to asonda only says you hung out with friends, not what you did. The polite version suits someone like Tanaka-san.

questions.english: When Kenji hears that his mom took piano lessons too, what does he ask her?
questions.ja: ケンジさんは、お母さんに何と聞きましたか？
questions.kana: けんじさんは、おかあさんになんとききましたか？
questions.romaji: kenji-san wa, okaasan ni nan to kikimashita ka?

choices.english: Mom, you can play the piano?
Mom, you can play around on the piano?

questions.explanation: Line 8: okaasan, piano hikeru no? Hiku is the verb for actually playing a keyboard or string instrument, and hikeru is 'can play'. His mom answers with the same word (line 9: hikeru yo). A carries suru over from sports and games (sakkaa shinai no?, geemu shiteru). With an instrument, suru or yaru only names it as a hobby, and it doesn't ask whether she can play. C is English 'play' turned into asobu, which means playing around or having fun; you don't asobu an instrument.

questions.english: Mai hears you play a few bars on a piano and asks, "e, piano hikeru no?" (Wait, you can play the piano?) Tell her you took piano lessons back in the day.
questions.answer: Say you used to take lessons, using piano with narau in its -teta form: un, mukashi piano naratteta n da.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, mukashi piano naratteta n da.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、昔ピアノ習ってたんだ。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I took piano lessons back in the day.

modelAnswers.romaji: piano wa mukashi naratteta kara, chotto hikeru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: ピアノは昔習ってたから、ちょっと弾けるよ。
modelAnswers.english: I took piano lessons years ago, so I can play a bit.

questions.explanation: Lessons with a teacher are narau, and naratteta is 'used to take lessons', as Kenji and his mom both say (line 5: mukashi naratteta n da kara; line 6: naratteta kedo; line 7: okaasan mo mukashi piano naratteta). Mai asked with hiku (hikeru no?), but narau tells her where the skill came from. Don't say piano o benkyou shita, which sounds like studying it as a school subject. Don't say oboeta either: that is picking something up by yourself, the way Okaasan picked up the game tune (line 11: oboechatta).

newWords.english: long ago, back in the day (mukashi naratteta = used to take lessons)
pick up, memorise (oboechatta = it stuck, I picked it up)
play around, have fun (not used for sports or instruments)
